We know one student got 95%.  
Another student got 3 wrong out of 40, so that student got 40 − 3 = 37 correct.  
Percentage for that student: (37/40) × 100 = 92.5%.  

The highest score so far is 95%.  
To beat that, Sierra needs more than 95%.  
If the test has 40 questions (since the second student’s score is out of 40), then:  
Let x be the number she gets right.  
We need (x/40) × 100 > 95 → x/40 > 0.95 → x > 38.  
Since x must be an integer, x = 39.  

So she needs 39 correct out of 40.

Final answer: Sierra
